caveat: Dropping years further reduces an already-small n (9 -> 7 years), so this is a qualitative sign-recovery test, not a precision estimate.
decision_rule: Bayesian autumn (S8) recovering positive and fPLS k=1 turning positive once storms are out indicates storm contamination and a real autumn window. Autumn positive surviving only in k=2 or k=3, with the storm years extreme on the top S8-contributing component (see fpls_component_attribution), indicates storm-fitting rather than a real signal. With fewer years remaining after the drop, fPLS k=3 is barely identified, so weight the k=1 and Bayesian sign-recovery over the k=3 behavior; anything that only moves at k=3 stays ambiguous.
